title: Blocks, Procs & Lambdas
intro: Blocks, procs, and lambdas are the most distinctively Ruby topic in any backend interview, and the one candidates most often get half-right. The four key differences between a Proc and a lambda — return behaviour, arity enforcement, the === operator, and lambda? — appear in almost every mid-level Ruby interview. This page covers the full picture: block syntax (do/end vs curly brace precedence), yield and block_given?, converting methods to procs with &method(:name), the stabby lambda syntax, closures and captured bindings, Proc#curry for partial application, and how Enumerable builds its entire API on top of a single block expectation. Every answer includes the idiomatic Ruby pattern — no verbose Java-style explicit returns.
